video.title: Can You Make Money With an AI App? Test This First

summary: The Dark Horse Entrepreneur host argues that AI makes building apps fast, but unvalidated apps still don't sell. Copying proven apps proves a market, not that anyone will switch to yours. He gives a five-step test: a micro-problem filter, a proof checklist of evidence that costs someone something, 'switch conversations' with 5-10 real users about past behaviour, a 'smallest paid promise' tested by pre-sale, manual delivery or a specific waitlist, and a build-or-don't-build decision against a pass mark written in advance. The worked example is a $5/month game-day confirmation text tool for youth cheer coaches.

ideas.name: Game-day confirmation text tool for youth cheer coaches (micro SaaS example)
ideas.one_liner: One-feature app that sends one message to parents and shows who has confirmed, for $5/month.
ideas.customer: Youth cheer coaches juggling about 12 parents
ideas.problem: Chasing parents one by one for game-day confirmations
ideas.offer: Single game-day text and confirmation dashboard

pricing.notes: Hypothetical: 100 coaches = $500 MRR. Test by pre-sale, by doing it by hand, or a specific waitlist.

acquisition_channels.details: Ask questions (not pitch) in coach groups and forums, respecting group rules.

ideas.delivery: Vibe-coded app; manual concierge test first.

acquisition.how: Community posts and SEO are inbound; sending marketing texts to parents needs their consent under UK PECR (the coach sends, so it's service messaging).

delivery.how: Software sends texts and tracks replies.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK for youth sports clubs; SMS costs and consent rules apply.

quotes.text: A game day text tool that lets your youth cheer coaches send one message to see which parents have confirmed without chasing 12 people manually by hand for five bucks a month
quotes.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

metric_claims.claim: Example micro SaaS: $5/month x 100 coaches = $500 MRR

quote.text: That's $5 a month MRR per customer. Get 100 coaches on this and you've got $500 a month in recurring revenue coming in
quote.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

metric_claims.claim: Experienced iOS dev built a mood tracker with AI in ~37 minutes (Starter Story)
Interview 5-10 people matching the buyer persona

quote.text: You're going to want to find five to 10 people who match your who, your buyer persona
quote.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

tactics.name: Micro-problem filter (pass 4 of 5)
steps: Who exactly has it (job title/situation)?
How often (weekly or better)?
What does it cost them (time, money, embarrassment, missed sales)?
Are they already paying to deal with it?
Can one feature fix the core?
Fill 'I want to build an app that does X to solve Y for Z'

tactics.name: Proof checklist (get 3+)
steps: Paid competitors exist (app stores, Product Hunt) with many reviews
People complaining in their own words on Reddit, Facebook groups, forums
1-star and 3-star reviews of competitors
Searches for '<competitor> alternative'
Homemade workarounds (spreadsheets, templates)
Copy exact quotes into a doc for sales copy

quote.text: One-star reviews tell you what people hate. Three-star reviews are going to tell you what they liked
quote.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

tactics.name: Switch conversation
steps: Find 5-10 persona matches where complaints live; ask questions, don't pitch
Ask about the past: walk me through the last time
What do you use now? What do you hate? What have you tried? What would make you switch?
Never ask 'would you use my app?'
Listen for heat and existing spend

quote.text: Please never ask that. Everyone is going to say yes
quote.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

tactics.name: Smallest paid promise
steps: One sentence: I help [person] do [one thing] without [pain] for [price]
Test via Stripe pre-sale page with ship date and full refund guarantee, do-it-by-hand service, or specific founding-price waitlist
Write the pass mark first (e.g. 3 strangers pay within 2 weeks)
Build if hit; else change one variable (price, person, feature) and retest

quote.text: If three coaches that I do not personally know pay or commit within the next 2 weeks, I'm going to build
quote.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

tactics.name: 15-minute review mining
steps: Pick the biggest competitor
Read 20 one-star and three-star reviews
Copy lines that make you think 'I can fix that'

tools_mentioned.name: Dark Horse Insider / AI Escape Plan newsletter

warnings.warning: AI makes building fast but doesn't make unwanted apps sell.

quote.text: AI made building fast. It did not make unwanted apps profitable for the maker
quote.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

warnings.warning: A proven market doesn't prove anyone will buy from you; you need a reason to switch.

quote.text: Proving a market exists is not the same as proving anybody will buy from you
quote.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

warnings.warning: Zero competitors and zero complaints usually means an empty road for a reason.

quote.text: most of the time it means it's really an empty road for a reason
quote.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

warnings.warning: Don't buy upvotes or game communities; it burns reputation with your customers.
YouTubers' income claims are their story, not your forecast.

quote.text: Don't go out there start treating it like your forecast
quote.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

warnings.warning: Don't let AI pretend to be a customer.

quote.text: But, it's not a customer. Never let it pretend to be one
quote.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

lessons.lesson: Validate demand before building; code is cheap but your evenings aren't.

quote.text: Code got cheap. Your evenings, they didn't get cheap
quote.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

lessons.lesson: Copying proven apps is fine if you have a specific reason customers would switch.
Evidence must cost someone something: money, time, workarounds, complaints.
Ask about past behaviour, not future intentions.

quote.text: You want to talk about the things they've actually done or are doing in the past, cuz that's where the truth lives
quote.speaker: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host

lessons.lesson: Pre-sell with refunds, or deliver by hand, before building.
Set the pass mark before testing to avoid moving goalposts.
Micro apps should solve one weekly-or-more pain with one feature.
Walking away after a failed two-week test is a win, not failure.

evidence_quality.rationale: Advice and framework with a hypothetical example; no first-hand app revenue.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Promotes his newsletters (AI Escape Plan, Dark Horse Insider).
